premises.text: Insurance brokers cannot legally rebate commissions, so Zenefits instead gives free HR/payroll/benefits software funded by those commissions
premises.evidence_span: it's illegal for them to rebate any portion of that commission to their clients. So I can't give you guys money back, but what I can do is provide a whole lot of services and software for free

premises.text: Platform connects existing payroll and benefits systems and can become broker of record with a simple online authorization
premises.evidence_span: You don't have to re enroll or switch anything you could just connect your existing systems to our platform

premises.text: Software automates hiring/onboarding paperwork, payroll setup, and benefits enrollment that is mostly administrative HR
premises.evidence_span: we can start to replace people and paper with software and technology

domains.name: free HR funded by insurance commissions

value.text: Companies get payroll, benefits, and HR admin handled for free while brokers/HR outsourcers are disrupted
value.evidence_span: we take on and manage all of your payroll, all of your benefits, all of the associated HR administrative work

causal_links.evidence_span: We do all of it for free, because we make money on the insurance commissions
we become the broker of record. And that does two things
the least amount of work that is physically possible to do for you to hire someone

notes: Free HR-as-service, broker economics, and illegal-rebate constraint folded as one commercial wedge (§4.1). Payroll/benefits connection and BOR letter as distribution/capture mechanism. Onboarding automation as product mechanism. Disruptive-competitor rhetoric treated as value/GTM consequence of those premises. Three-domain partition justified: commission-funded free offering, systems/BOR capture, and admin automation are separately revisable.
